pairs.note: Periplus §56, the pepper cargo manifest. PHASE2.md names this chunk explicitly as one of the three the ranking set must contain.

Second known-good for the same query. One query with three acceptable passages is three pairs, each scored on its own account, because a ranking that finds one of the three is not the same result as one that finds all three.
The hardest of the three: Old Tamil verse reached from an English prose question. Part 4 scored Old Tamil 0.368 against 0.6-0.7 for other scripts.

The hero demo for Classical Chinese retrieval. Held back from being more than this: the record's original_text_excerpt is known corrupt against Chen Shou 1975 (PROGRESS.md, Da Qin block §4), so this pair asserts the characters that are on disk, not the characters that ought to be.
36 characters. The shortest non-English chunk in the corpus, and therefore the one whose retrieval is most sensitive to index size - watch it hardest on the W2b curve.
PHASE2.md names the Vimose transliteration chunk explicitly. Proto-Norse in romanised transliteration, 110 characters.

The question that was correctly REFUSED at the Phase 1 exit gate while the system held the evidence. Its ranking is the thing to watch: if the passage ranks well here, the exit-gate failure was in answering and not in retrieval, which is the persevere verdict's central claim.

The other half of the discriminator: the rewording that WORKED against byte-identical evidence. PHASE2.md names the Adulis export chunk explicitly. observed_chunk_id is original::002 and this sentence now lives in original::005 - the drift that made chunk-id keying unusable is on this pair.

same_language. One Tamil chunk in the corpus, so a pass here is thin evidence and a fail is strong evidence.

cross_lingual. The hardest case in the corpus.

The same-query-two-languages test from the Phase 1 plan. A pair is meaningful only against its partner: if the two members rank the same passage differently, the shared embedding space is doing less work than claimed.

The only Part 6 probe that already carried expect_text_contains, and the reason this file asserts on characters rather than on ids.

The passage was already chosen in Part 6; the query is written here to reach it. Targets §29, not the §27-28 chunks, so a pair that lands on the neighbouring section of the same document is a miss and says so.
Nabataean Aramaic in transliteration. 206 characters, and the chunk is mostly editorial framing - a hard retrieval target for an honest reason.
79 characters of Sabaic in transliteration - the shortest chunk in the corpus. If the W2b curve has a cliff, this is where it should appear first.
